title.value: Deep Neural Networks pruning via the Structured Perspective Regularization
title.justification: The title was extracted directly from the beginning of the document, indicating the main subject and method introduced in the paper.
title.quote: Deep Neural Networks pruning via the Structured Perspective Regularization

extractions.description: The paper proposes a novel method for pruning deep neural networks called Structured Perspective Regularization (SPR). This method is based on operational research tools, specifically using mixed-integer programming and perspective reformulation, to better structure the pruning process of the network during training. The technique is applied to ResNet architectures on standard datasets, showing competitive performance.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving neural network efficiency in terms of training and usage, primarily for computational and storage benefits, rather than addressing climate or ecologically-related sustainable development issues directly.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In Machine Learning, Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are a very powerful tool, broadly used in many applications. Often, the selected (deep) architectures include many layers, and therefore a large amount of parameters, which makes training, storage and inference expensive. This motivated a stream of research about compressing the original networks into smaller ones without excessively sacrificing performances.

primary_category.justification: The research described focuses on computational efficiency and the performance of neural networks. While this could indirectly benefit energy savings, it is not explicitly tied to climate or ecologically related applications, which is necessary to classify it under these specific categories.
primary_category.quote: This motivated a stream of research about compressing the original networks into smaller ones without excessively sacrificing performances.

secondary_categories.justification: There is no secondary emphasis on climate or ecological sustainability themes within the paper. The content is highly technical and rooted in machine learning algorithm efficiency.
secondary_categories.quote: The striking practical success of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) has been initially driven by the ability of adding more and more parameters to the models, which has led to vastly increased accuracy. This brute-force approach, however, has numerous drawbacks: besides the ever-present risk of overfitting, massive models are costly to store and run.

primary_sub_category.justification: The focus of the paper is on pruning neural networks to make them more efficient, which falls outside the realm of the defined sub-categories aimed at directly impacting sustainability goals.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a new pruning method based on Operational Research tools. We start from a natural Mixed-Integer-Programming model for the problem, and we use the Perspective Reformulation technique to strengthen its continuous relaxation.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There is no mention or inference of secondary climate or sustainable-related sub-categories addressed by the paper. The research scope is technical and pertains mainly to algorithmic improvements in ANN.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Pruning can be performed while training or after training. The advantage of the latter is the ability of using standard training techniques un-modified, which may lead to better performances.

applications.value: Improved efficiency and performance of ANN through structured pruning
applications.justification: The paper's application focus is on enhancing computational efficiency of neural networks, which can have broader implications for technology and systems utilizing these networks in various fields.
applications.quote: Loosely speaking, pruning requires finding the best compromise between removing some of the elements of the ANN (weights, channels, filters, layers, blocks, . . . ) and the decrease in accuracy that this could bring.

new_primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is specific to computational optimization and does not introduce a new category relevant to climate or ecological sustainability.
new_primary_category.quote: The paper proposes a novel method for pruning deep neural networks called Structured Perspective Regularization.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no introduction of a new sub-category that ties the research to sustainable development as per the topics provided.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our approach is therefore principled, being grounded on an exact model rather than based on heuristic score functions to decide what entities to prune as prevalent in the literature so far.
